chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayoub, from Abu Al-Maghra', from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever kills his slave deliberately, then upon him is that he should emancipate a neck, and that he should feed sixty poor persons, and fast for two months consecutively.
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for killing a slave deliberately in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific expiation (kaffarah) for a master who deliberately kills his slave, emphasizing a triad of penalties: freeing a slave, feeding sixty poor people, and fasting for two consecutive months. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling highlights the high status of slaves as property with rights, distinguishing it from general homicide, and underscores the social responsibility of the wealthy through the feeding component.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Abu Al Magra, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who kills his slave deliberately, so upon him is that he should emancipate a neck, and that he should feed sixty poor (persons), and Fasts for two months consecutively’.
